coordinateUnits: percent of complete uncropped image; top-left origin

steps.title: Start with what Chris already knows.
steps.explanation: Bring existing customer notes into the onboarding workflow instead of reconstructing discovery across a new set of fields.
steps.chrisValue: Less repeated preparation before a customer can get started.
steps.alt: Chris prototype view: Start with what Chris already knows.

steps.title: Turn discovery into a plan people can use.
steps.explanation: The draft connects engineering problems to technical goals and a proposed first milestone, giving Chris something concrete to assess.
steps.chrisValue: Less work translating customer conversations into an onboarding plan.
steps.alt: Chris prototype view: Turn discovery into a plan people can use.

steps.title: Save preparation time. Keep customer judgment.
steps.explanation: Chris can edit the draft and save changes before publishing. He can correct the interpretation while the relevant source context remains visible.
steps.chrisValue: A faster starting point that Chris can tailor before sharing.
steps.alt: Chris prototype view: Save preparation time. Keep customer judgment.

steps.title: Give the champion a goal worth sharing.
steps.explanation: The customer-facing experience carries the published goal and first milestone into Portal, giving the champion a common starting point for the team.
steps.chrisValue: Chris’s customer understanding survives the handoff.
steps.alt: Champion prototype view: Give the champion a goal worth sharing.

steps.title: Let the champion coordinate from recorded progress.
steps.explanation: The team view brings milestone completion, blockers and open questions together. In this recording these counts are still zero.
steps.chrisValue: The champion has a place to check team status before asking Chris to reconstruct it.
steps.alt: Champion prototype view: Let the champion coordinate from recorded progress.

steps.title: Give developers a relevant place to begin.
steps.explanation: The developer sees the team’s engineering goal alongside a specific opportunity: record who owns payments-api’s code. The suggested work is connected to the customer objective.
steps.chrisValue: A clearer starting point reduces the need for Chris to explain every next step.
steps.alt: Developer prototype view: Give developers a relevant place to begin.

steps.title: Keep technical questions close to the work.
steps.explanation: The AiKA-style prototype surface exposes context choices for onboarding, selected work, repository observations and team progress. This demonstrates the intended handoff to contextual assistance.
steps.chrisValue: A path toward resolving routine questions without making Chris the first stop.
steps.alt: Developer prototype view: Keep technical questions close to the work.

steps.title: Give Chris a basis for a useful follow-up.
steps.explanation: The customer progress view brings the goal, milestone and recorded activity together. This demo shows no recorded adoption yet; it illustrates the information Chris can monitor as work is reported.
steps.chrisValue: A shared view of customer progress can help Chris decide what to ask and where to support.
steps.alt: Chris prototype view: Give Chris a basis for a useful follow-up.
